newsitem.title: GERMANY: FAG says in talks on Hanover airport stake.
newsitem.headline: FAG says in talks on Hanover airport stake.

text.p: Flughafen Frankfurt/Main AG (FAG) said it is in initial talks about taking a stake of up to 30 percent in Hanover airport (HAJ).
FAG spokesman Klaus Busch told Reuters "We are holding talks. We are very interested, in the same way that we are interested in cooperation with other German airports."
But FAG, which owns and manages Frankfurt airport, was not yet in official negotiations on a financial stake, he added.

Flughafen Hannover-Langenhagen GmbH, whose 60 million mark capital is held in equal shares by the state of Lower Saxony and the city of Hanover, is to be turned into a joint-stock company, and then partially privatised.
A subsidiary of the Union Bank of Switzerland (UBS) has been commissioned to find purchasers for a 30 percent stake.
Busch stressed FAG did not want to dominate other German airports but to co-operate for mutual economic benefit.
"We say that it makes sense for FAG and other (German) airports to work together instead of BAA getting a foot in the door here," he said.
"That would certainly not be in the interests of other German airports since traffic would be siphoned off long-term to London Heathrow," he added.
BAA Plc runs Heathrow, Gatwick, Stansted and four other British airports.
In January, FAG spent a reported 7.6 million marks on buying a strategic 51 percent stake in Saarbruecken Airport from the Saarland state government.

FAG chairman Dr Wilhelm Bender said at the time some services could be moved from Frankfurt and measures would be undertaken to win back passengers and air cargo shippers who had switched to using other large European airports. - Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax:5017
